articles.title: Latest Heisman Trophy 2026 Odds as Arch Manning, Jeremiah Smith Rise
articles.summary: A few of the Heisman Trophy's greatest contenders took centerstage on Saturday, and they acquitted themselves well in the race's very early stages.
articles.body:
A few of the Heisman Trophy's greatest contenders took centerstage on Saturday, and they acquitted themselves well in the race's very early stages.

Here's a look at the latest odds for the top 10 contenders following the 3:30 p.m. ET set of games via FanDuel Sportsbook .

Five of those 10 players took the field Saturday. Here's how they did.

Texas quarterback Arch Manning began his second season as the Longhorns' starter by completing 20-of-27 passes for 305 yards, four touchdowns and one interception in a 59-7 home win over Texas State. Two of the TD passes went to Cam Coleman (six and 20 yards).

Manning's day was done with 7:55 left in the third quarter after he found Hollywood Smothers for a 13-yard touchdown pass to put Texas up 41-7.

He and the No. 5 Longhorns have a tougher test next week when the Longhorns host the No. 1 Ohio State Buckeyes in a rematch of last year's season opener, when OSU won 14-7. However, a strong showing from Manning could absolutely vault him into the early Heisman lead.

Speaking of the Buckeyes, Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith caught eight passes for 151 yards and two touchdowns in the first half alone to lead the No. 1 Buckeyes to a 56-3 home win over Ball State to begin the season.

Smith was sensational, making a 48-yard touchdown catch in air-tight coverage to open the scoring.

He also got a nifty toe-tap touchdown in the final seconds of the second quarter to put OSU up 27-3.

Since 2000, 21 quarterbacks have won the Heisman compared to just three running backs, one wide receiver and one two-way player. However, Smith is making a great case that he deserves the Heisman.

OSU quarterback Julian Sayin, of course, connected with Smith on those touchdowns. Sayin was about as good as one can get, completing 21-of-25 passes for 320 yards and three touchdowns (no picks).

His day was done early in the third quarter after his 13-yard pass to Bo Jackson set up the running back's 65-yard TD rush.

Oregon quarterback Dante Moore had a great day, completing 28-of-37 passes for 378 yards and three touchdowns in a 34-27 home win over the Boise State Broncos.

The No. 2 Ducks survived a serious upset attempt, though, as BSU was up 17-7 early.

However, Oregon scored 17 straight points for a 24-17 lead and later took a 34-27 advantage after Dante Moore and wide receiver Dakorien Moore, who showcased a tremendous effort, connected on a 62-yard touchdown.

Lastly, Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover had big cleats to fill after Heisman Trophy winner and national champion Fernando Mendoza left for the NFL, but he got off to a fantastic start, connecting on 13-of-16 passes for 231 yards and four touchdowns in a 52-16 home win over North Texas.

Hoover got busted up during the game after drawing a face mask penalty, but that didn't stop him from playing.

Ultimately, one of every four of Hoover's throws resulted in a touchdown pass.

Hoover and the Hoosiers will now face Howard on Saturday at noon ET.

articles.title: Jayden Daniels Excluded from LSU Video Highlighting Former Tigers in NFL After No. 5 Jersey Dispute
articles.summary: Washington Commanders quarterback and former LSU standout Jayden Daniels wasn't included in the Tigers' video highlighting the school's NFL players ahead of a matchup with Clemson on Saturday.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders quarterback and former LSU standout Jayden Daniels wasn't included in the Tigers' video highlighting the school's NFL players ahead of a matchup with Clemson on Saturday.

LSU alumni in the NFL who were featured in the video included Joe Burrow, Justin Jefferson, Ja'Marr Chase, Malik Nabers, Will Campbell, Patrick Queen, Mansoor Delane and Garrett Nussmeier.

Daniels, who wore No. 5 at LSU, previously sent the school a cease-and-desist letter that stemmed from the decision to allow cornerback D.J. Pickett to wear the same number on his jersey this season.

Daniels only played two seasons at LSU from 2022-23, but earned Heisman Trophy honors during his second year with the team.

articles.title: Go for it or not? Dave Aranda's 2-point decision that led to Baylor's loss to Auburn won't lose him his job, but he's running out of time regardless
articles.summary: You'd be hard-pressed to find anyone at Baylor who disagreed with Aranda's decision to go for two and a victory over Auburn. But not getting it still carries...
articles.body:
ATLANTA — Whenever Baylor has to make the ultimate call on Dave Aranda, it is unlikely to be clear-cut. He is too competent to crater and too well-liked to author his own demise, working at a school that would prefer not to buy out a football coach unless it has to.

But it is not a secret, least of all to Aranda, that his seventh season will be defined by decisions: The little ones he makes every week, followed by the big one his employer must render.

After the first of 12 data points is now in the rear-view mirror, it's imperative to start thinking about the question that can bring some of these fine margins into leader focus: How much credit does a coach get for doing the right thing but getting the wrong result?

Though perhaps not every fan would agree, you'd be hard-pressed to find anyone within the Baylor program who disagreed with Aranda's decision to go for two and a victory over Auburn on Saturday night after his quarterback, DJ Lagway, fought through an ankle sprain and threw a touchdown pass with nine seconds remaining.

Analytically, it was the right call. Emotionally, it was a risk worth taking. Practically, it was a no-brainer.

"There was no hesitation," Aranda said. "The book said to go for it, but it wasn't so much that. We had so many guys that were just doing everything they can to try to push through and close the game out. I just didn't feel playing longer was going to benefit us.

In the end, no matter how the season turns out, there will always be a what-if attached to Auburn 17, Baylor 16 . The 2-point play that offensive coordinator Jake Spavital drew up worked. Lagway made the throw, tight end Matthew Klopfenstein caught the ball and had what seemed to be a path to the end zone.

He just couldn't get there before Auburn safety Eric Winters wrapped him in a textbook tackle, getting him on the ground a mere inches from the goal line.

"I thought he was in," Aranda said. "You hear the call, you know what the play is, you're watching for it and you see it. I'm thinking it's points. For it not to be just sucks."

Five years ago, Aranda was on the opposite side of a similar play in a much more significant moment. In the 2021 Big 12 championship game, with just seconds to play, Oklahoma State had a fourth-down play at the 1-yard line to win the game. Running back Dezmon Jackson had what seemed to be a sure touchdown running for the corner of the end zone but felt the pressure from behind, reached for the pylon and came up tantalizingly short.

At that moment, Aranda's career seemed like a rocket ship. In his second year as a head coach, he had won a conference title, followed by beating Ole Miss in the Sugar Bowl. If anything, Baylor would've been concerned that he might end up getting lured back to a place like LSU, where he won a national title as defensive coordinator.

But since then, Aranda has posted three losing seasons in four years. Some of the issues were of his own making. Others, like Baylor ranking in the lower-tier of NIL spending in the Big 12, have been institutional obstacles.

The bottom line, though, is Baylor's attendance has cratered and there have not been enough quality wins to secure his future. Last November, in the midst of losing five out of six to end the season and athletic director Mack Rhoades resigning due to personal issues, Baylor announced that Aranda would return so that a new athletic director could come in and assess the football program.

That new athletic director is Doug McNamee, who previously worked at Baylor and left to work for Magnolia, the company founded by Chip and Joanna Gaines, who are among the school's biggest benefactors.

From now until the end of the season, taking the temperature of Baylor's key stakeholders is the reality McNamee will live every day. It's hard to imagine that a game like Saturday makes the picture any clearer.

Yes, Baylor fought hard, had an outstanding defensive game plan to bottle up Auburn's offense and made one clutch play after another on the 75-yard drive that gave the Bears a chance to win it with a 2-point conversion. To go for it in that moment, knowing the stakes, knowing the fragility of his tenure, is the kind of coaching that shows the courage of his convictions.

"We had nothing in our mind but next play," said receiver Gavin Freeman, who caught a touchdown on fourth-and-goal from the 5-yard line. "No matter what happens, just keep going. I have faith in my guys and we all had faith going forward because that's what we do in practice. That's what we practice all the time is winning the game."

But is that enough when it doesn't work?

As much as you can commend Aranda for almost getting off to an ideal start in a make-or-break year, this was not a game Baylor should not have lost.

When you have 436 offensive yards, you should score more than 16 points. When your defense forces three turnovers, you should capitalize. When you leave points on the board by missing a 42-yard field goal, then calling an ill-fated fourth down play in the third quarter instead of a 33-yard field goal in a game you lost by a single point, can you really say the head coach had a good day?

"Mistakes. That's why we lost," Aranda said. "That's what I told the team. Early in the game there's too many opportunities we had to finish drives, to put points on the board, and we didn't do it. I take the credit for that. I should have done a better job of coaching that. More games are lost than won, especially early in the season, and I could've communicated that better because I think we contributed to that tonight."

As always, Aranda was forthright, cerebral and emotionally even-keeled. It's part of what makes him hard to get your arms around. He is not a natural salesman, and Baylor's fan base has largely registered its vote on him last year with all the empty seats in McLane Stadium.

Baylor played with heart and grit Saturday, but Aranda can only change their minds by winning. Making the right call or coming close — even inches short — won't be good enough.

images.caption: Baylor coach Dave Aranda reacts to a play during his team's loss to Auburn. (Andrew J. Clark/Getty Images) (Andrew J. Clark/ISI Photos via Getty Images)

articles.title: Bryce Underwood, No. 16 Michigan Avoid WMU Upset Bid on Hail Mary, Final Box Score Stats, Highlights
articles.summary: Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood uncorked a 47-yard Hail Mary pass that landed in wide receiver JJ Buchanan's hands for a game-winning touchdown with no time remaining as the No. 16 Wolverines survived a tremendous upset attempt from the visiting Western Michigan Broncos and won 13-12.
articles.body:
Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood uncorked a 47-yard Hail Mary pass that landed in wide receiver JJ Buchanan's hands for a game-winning touchdown with no time remaining as the No. 16 Wolverines survived a tremendous upset attempt from the visiting Western Michigan Broncos and won 13-12.

Michigan was a monstrous 27.5-point favorite heading into this game, per FanDuel Sportsbook . However, the Wolverines' offense couldn't get anything going between the touchdown-scoring opening drive and the final play. That didn't matter, though, as the Wolverines ultimately came through with the big win.

This game won't be without controversy, however. On the penultimate play , Underwood threw a Hail Mary that went through the end zone and into a throng of players that was navigating out of bounds.

Upon further review, it appeared the game clock hit zero before the pass was deflected off any players, meaning the game should have ended.

Sports journalist and writer Rodger Sherman of the Sports! newsletter notably edited the video of the play , and the ball is just a few feet away from coming in contact with anyone on the field.

It initially appeared that Western Michigan won the game, and the Broncos began celebrating. After an official review, however, referees put one second back on the clock. That led to Underwood's Hail Mary miracle and Michigan's great escape.

NBC rules analyst Terry McAulay questioned how Big Ten officials arrived at the conclusion that there was one second left on the clock.

People will be talking about the final second of the game for years, but there were (officially) 59 minutes and 59 seconds of game action before then as well.

Michigan's offense looked crisp to start thanks to an 11-play, 75-yard drive capped by Underwood's one-yard touchdown leap on 4th-and-goal.

However, Michigan's offense went completely stagnant from there thanks in large part to a great WMU defensive effort. The Wolverines' next four drives went a combined 26 yards and ended in punts.

Michigan's last first half drive was calamitous. The Wolverines had the ball on their own 27-yard line with nine seconds left and little chance to score but decided to throw the ball. WMU linebacker Dillon Moore came up with a pick, and Kelly hit a 45-yard field goal with no time left.

Both teams traded punts to start the third quarter, but Western Michigan then engineered a 20-play, 71-yard drive that took nearly an entire quarter's worth of time (13:40 to be exact) off the clock. Kelly's 39-yard field goal gave WMU a 9-7 lead with 10:25 left.

Both teams traded punts again, but WMU was winning the field position battle and pinned Michigan on its own seven-yard line with 3:04 remaining.

Three plays later, Underwood ran for 13 yards to the Michigan 31, but WMU defensive back Joshua Franklin forced a fumble, recovered by teammate KJ Burley.

The Broncos had a chance to run the clock out on their next drive and had a 3rd-and-2 on the Michigan 12-yard line, but a fumbled snap (which they recovered) led to a two-yard loss. Kelly hit his fourth field goal, this time from 33 yards out.

Michigan's final drive started with two incomplete passes, but Underwood found Buchanan for a 28-yard strike on 3rd-and-10. He then spiked the ball, leading to the final two plays.

This game served as Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham's debut with the team. Whittingham, who was Utah's head coach from 2005-2025 before arriving in Ann Arbor, couldn't have scripted a more dramatic start.

He spoke after the game about the emotion of the moment, the issues Michigan encountered during the matchup and the infamous second left on the clock.

WMU head coach Lance Taylor took the high road when asked about what happened at the end of the game.

The biggest question, of course, is what the officials saw leading to there being one second left.

As of late Saturday night into early Sunday morning, there was no word, although reporters requested a pool report (i.e. a designated media member speaks with a game official regarding a matter).

It appears, though, that officials won't be speaking on the matter.

One can guess that the ending to this game will be much-discussed in the ensuing days. It'll certainly go down in history.

Michigan Stadium isn't immune to Hail Mary passes. In 1979, Michigan wideout Anthony Carter hauled one in to beat Indiana, 27-21. In 1994, Colorado quarterback Kordell Stewart found wide receiver Michael Westbrook to beat Michigan, 27-26. It's not immune to major upsets either, as then Division I-FCS Appalachian State notably beat No. 5 Michigan 34-32 in 2007.

This time around, Michigan found itself on the right side of Hail Mary history while avoiding another historical upset.

Looking ahead, WMU and Michigan move along to Saturday's Week 2 contests.

The Wolverines will remain home next Saturday but will take on an extremely tough No. 10 Oklahoma squad, which opened the season with a 51-0 win over UTEP.

The Broncos will return home to host Monmouth.

articles.title: Western Michigan coach: 'I know when I looked up at the clock, it was past zeroes before we touched it' ahead of Michigan's controversial Hail Mary
articles.summary: Officials added a second back onto the clock before Michigan converted a second-chance Hail Mary for a 13-12 win.
articles.body:
Western Michigan coach Lance Taylor believes the clock was at zero when his team forced Michigan's Hail Mary to fall incomplete.

The No. 16 Wolverines got a second chance at a Hail Mary after officials controversially added a second back onto the clock and made the most of that second when JJ Buchanan caught the pass from Bryce Underwood for a 13-12 win.

WMU appeared to have escaped with a 12-7 upset win after Underwood's pass didn't touch a WMU player who had stepped out of bounds until there was no time remaining on the clock. However, officials ruled after a replay review that there was, somehow, still one second remaining.

After the game, Taylor was asked in his news conference about the play. He was diplomatic and said that it was also an opportunity for his defense.

"I have not seen the clip, several people have mentioned it to me that the game was over. I think one, [MAC commissioner Jon Steinbrecher] has already reached out. Normally he handles those type of situations and reviews. I thought that the crew tonight did a really nice job handling multiple close calls and review situations. We had several where the spot was questioned and reviewed and those calls went our way, the review went our way. So, listen, I'll let our commissioner and those guys handle it. "At the end of the day, you don't always control those situations or is there a second left on the clock — we talk a lot about just respond, regardless of what the circumstances are. We can't control whether there's a second left on the clock or not. We went out the first time, we defended perfectly the Hail Mary situation. I thought our guys did an excellent job. I know when I looked up at the clock, it was past zeroes before we touched it. I knew they'd review it, it was the last play of the game and because we defended it so well wasn't worried or concerned about our guys going out and defending it the second time, and unfortunately we did not defend it as well the second time. A little bit different — the first time he threw it towards the back of the goal line and out of bounds, the second attempt he threw it towards the front of the goal line and the receiver went up and made a nice play and was able to get into the end zone and I think that's a good lesson for our defense. We can't just box out the back of the end zone. We've got to make sure we cover them up at the front pylon as well. So we'll learn from that and grow and I'm sure I'll watch the TV copy now."

Western Michigan had the ball for over 40 minutes of game time as it tried to limit Michigan's possessions. The strategy worked for much of the night. After Underwood fumbled with 1:40 to go, WMU added a field goal to make it a five-point lead with 35 seconds to go.

But Underwood hit Buchanan for 28 yards on third down with 11 seconds to go to get the Wolverines into WMU territory. That play then set up what could become one of the most famous Michigan plays of all time. And one that the Big Ten's replay crew will need to explain thoroughly to convince most non-Michigan fans that the game clock should have been adjusted.

articles.title: Manchester United XI vs Everton – Predicted lineup and team news
articles.summary: Manchester United can move to two wins from three opening games when they travel to Everton on Sunday. Michael Carrick’s side sit tenth in the table after re...
articles.body:
Manchester United can move to two wins from three opening games when they travel to Everton on Sunday.

Michael Carrick's side sit tenth in the table after recovering from an opening-day defeat at Hull City with a 5-2 win over Ipswich Town. Sunday is the 20th Premier League game of Carrick's second spell in charge of United, a period in which no side has won more points (42) than the Red Devils.

Victory would take him to 45 points from those 20 games, a tally matched by only four other managers in the competition's history: Jose Mourinho and Antonio Conte at Chelsea, John Gregory at Aston Villa, and Arne Slot at Liverpool.

Carlos Baleba, United's summer signing, remains sidelined with an ankle injury that will keep him out for a couple more weeks, while Manuel Ugarte (knee) and Amad Diallo (ankle) are also long-term absentees. Tom Heaton and Matthijs de Ligt are both doubts, with de Ligt continuing to build up his training load following a long-term back issue.

There is better news on Luke Shaw and Mason Mount, both of whom are back in full training and available for selection. Carrick confirmed Mount's return personally: "Mase is back around the group, which was great. Trained this week, so that's a big positive for us."

Bruno Fernandes, who scored a hat-trick against Ipswich to take his season tally to three goals — more than any other player in the division so far this season — is expected to continue behind Matheus Cunha, with Marcus Rashford and Bryan Mbeumo completing the front line.

Manchester United possible starting XI (4-2-3-1): Lammens; Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Shaw; Mainoo, Tielemans; Mbeumo, Fernandes, Rashford; Cunha

The Premier League match kicks off at 14:00 on Sunday, 6 September 2026.

How to watch Everton vs Manchester United?

The match will be broadcast live on Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports Premier League in the UK, with coverage beginning from 1pm.

articles.title: Barcelona XI vs Valencia – Predicted lineup and team news
articles.summary: Barcelona are set to face Valencia in their upcoming La Liga fixture on Sunday, aiming to extend their impressive winning streak at the start of the new camp...
articles.body:
Barcelona are set to face Valencia in their upcoming La Liga fixture on Sunday, aiming to extend their impressive winning streak at the start of the new campaign.

Hansi Flick's Barcelona have made a flawless beginning to the league season, securing victories in all three matches played so far. The Blaugrana kicked things off with a dominant 5-0 away win over Elche CF, followed by a composed 2-0 success at home against Athletic Club. Last weekend, they continued their attacking prowess with a thrilling 5-2 home victory over Rayo Vallecano, reinforcing their position as early frontrunners for the title.

Heading into the clash at Mestalla, Barcelona are in high spirits, bolstered by several key squad updates.

A significant administrative win came as high-profile summer arrivals Gabriel Jesus and goalkeeper Dominik Livaković were officially registered and included in the matchday squad.

In midfield, the return of Gavi after a long absence brings both emotional and tactical benefits to Flick's setup.

There was a moment of concern when young star Lamine Yamal sat out a full training session due to a slight knock, but Flick has confirmed that the winger is fully fit and expected to feature in the starting lineup.

On the injury front, Frenkie de Jong and Roony Bardghji remain sidelined with knee problems, while academy talent Jesse Bisiwu is also unavailable.

Despite these absences, Barcelona possess considerable depth across the squad. Joan Garcia is anticipated to take his place between the posts, while the attacking line is likely to be led by Raphinha, supported by Yamal and Fermín López.

Possible Barcelona starting XI: J Garcia; E Garcia, Cubarsi, Martin, Espart; Pedri, Bernal; Yamal, Fermin, Gordon; Raphinha

The match will kick off at 3:15pm BST on Sunday, 6th September.

Fans in the UK can watch the Valencia vs Barcelona La Liga encounter live on Premier Sports 2.

articles.title: Everton vs Manchester United – Match preview and team news
articles.summary: Everton and Manchester United meet at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Sunday, with the hosts unbeaten after two matches and the visitors looking to build on a firs...
articles.body:
Everton and Manchester United meet at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Sunday, with the hosts unbeaten after two matches and the visitors looking to build on a first win of the season.

David Moyes's Everton sit seventh with four points, while Michael Carrick's United are tenth on three points having bounced back from an opening-day defeat to Hull City with a 5-2 win over Ipswich Town.

United have won each of the last four meetings between these two clubs, including both fixtures last season by an identical 1-0 scoreline, and a repeat result would take Moyes to within one defeat of equalling Harry Redknapp's Premier League record of 24 losses against the Red Devils.

Carrick, meanwhile, could move level with an elite group of five managers to have collected 45 or more points from their first 20 league games in a single spell at a club, a list that includes Jose Mourinho and Antonio Conte at Chelsea.

Both clubs endured a chaotic deadline day: Everton sold Iliman Ndiaye to Manchester City and saw a proposed deal for Folarin Balogun collapse, but brought back Jack Grealish on loan from the same City side.

Everton vs Manchester United – Match preview and team news

Last meeting: Everton 0-1 Manchester United (Premier League, 23 February 2026)

Christian Norgaard is the club's only confirmed absentee. Jack Grealish is in line to start on the left having returned on a season-long loan from Manchester City on deadline day, in the same swap that saw Iliman Ndiaye join City in the opposite direction. Brennan Johnson is set to take up the creative role vacated by Ndiaye's exit.

Carlos Baleba, Manuel Ugarte and Amad Diallo are all ruled out through injury, while Tom Heaton and Matthijs de Ligt remain doubts. There is better news on Luke Shaw and Mason Mount, both back in full training and available for selection, with Michael Carrick saying of Mount: "He's back around the group, which was great. Trained this week, so that's a big positive for us."

Everton remain unbeaten this season, beating Crystal Palace 2-0 before drawing 1-1 at Bournemouth thanks to a stoppage-time James Tarkowski header. Thierno Barry has been a persistent goal threat without finding the net, generating more non-penalty expected goals than any Premier League player this season bar Bryan Mbeumo and Alexander Isak.

Manchester United have recovered from an opening-day defeat at Hull City to beat Ipswich Town 5-2, with captain Bruno Fernandes scoring a hat-trick to take his tally to three goals this season, the most of any player in the division. United have conceded the first goal in both of their league games so far, and have not started a Premier League season conceding first in three straight matches since their title-winning 2012-13 campaign.

Everton predicted XI (4-2-3-1): Pickford; O'Brien, Tarkowski, Branthwaite, Mykolenko; Garner, Armstrong; Johnson, Dewsbury-Hall, Grealish; Barry

Manchester United predicted XI (4-2-3-1): Lammens; Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Shaw; Mainoo, Tielemans; Mbeumo, Fernandes, Rashford; Cunha

How to watch Everton vs Manchester United?

The match will be broadcast live in the United Kingdom on Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports Premier League, with coverage beginning from 1pm.

articles.body:
Everton will look to extend their unbeaten start to the season when Manchester United visit Hill Dickinson Stadium on Sunday.

David Moyes's side sit seventh in the table after a win and a draw from their opening two fixtures. Sunday's game is also personal for Moyes, who managed United between 2013 and 2014 and has since lost 23 Premier League meetings against his old club — one shy of Harry Redknapp's record of 24 defeats against the Red Devils in the competition.

Christian Norgaard remains the club's only confirmed absentee. There is no other fresh fitness concern in the squad heading into Sunday, though deadline day brought significant change: Iliman Ndiaye departed for Manchester City in a reported £65m deal, and a proposed move for Folarin Balogun from Monaco collapsed after the American forward pulled out of the deal following his medical.

Jack Grealish returned to the club on a season-long loan from Manchester City on the same day Ndiaye left, and is set to start on the left in place of Tyrique George after the winger's underwhelming display at Bournemouth. Brennan Johnson is expected to fill the creative role vacated by Ndiaye, while Ainsley Maitland-Niles, also signed on deadline day from Lyon, is likely to feature from the bench having yet to make his debut.

Everton possible starting XI (4-2-3-1): Pickford; O'Brien, Tarkowski, Branthwaite, Mykolenko; Garner, Armstrong; Johnson, Dewsbury-Hall, Grealish; Barry

articles.title: Western Michigan robbed of upset on Wolverines' Hail Mary | Reactions
articles.summary: The Western Michigan Broncos got a raw deal, losing to Michigan in very controversial fashion in Ann Arbor after one second was added to the clock.
articles.body:
The Western Michigan Broncos got a raw deal, losing to the Michigan Wolverines in very controversial fashion in Ann Arbor after one second was added to the clock.

Given a second chance at a game-ending Hail Mary despite the clock reaching 0:00 as the pass sailed out of the end zone on the previous play, Bryce Underwood found JJ Buchanan for a 47-yard touchdown pass.

No. 16 Michigan escaped with a 13-12 win against WMU.

It was Wolverines head coach Kyle Whittingham's debut at the school. Michigan was a 27.5-point favorite against its game Mid-American Conference opponent.

articles.title: No. 16 Michigan beats Western Michigan 13-12 on controversial Hail Mary after clock was reset to 1 second
articles.summary: Michigan made the most of its extra play
articles.body:
No. 16 Michigan avoided an upset loss to Western Michigan on Saturday night with a lot of help from instant replay.

Bryce Underwood hit JJ Buchanan for an incredible 47-yard Hail Mary as time expired for a 13-12 win. The pass came after the ball was snapped with one second left after Underwood's previous Hail Mary appeared to fall incomplete with no time remaining.

After a short review, a second was added back to the clock. And then Buchanan made the catch.

NBC's numerous replays of the first Hail Mary showed that the ball was not close to touching a Western Michigan player who had stepped out of bounds when he jumped for the pass until the clock showed 0:00. Rules analyst and former referee Terry McAuley was unable to come up with a concrete explanation for why a second was added to the clock.

"The ball isn't even close to touching the player when it goes to zero," McAuley said after he told viewers that he was informed that the clock on the bottom left of the screen was the stadium clock and in sync with the replay. "Now their Hawk Eye system apparently either was — had a different sync or whatever and they came up with one second when it touched the players. I don't see how that happened assuming our clock is correct. It is clearly not touching the player. It is clearly still in the air when the clock goes to zero on our screen. So the Big Ten's going to have to tell a lot of us how did they get to one second on this play."

Here's how the first Hail Mary looked in real time.

The second-chance Hail Mary was Buchanan's second massive catch of the final drive. He was responsible for all 75 yards on the drive as he caught a 28-yard pass on third down to get Michigan across midfield and put the Wolverines in position to go for the end zone.

Michigan got the ball back for its final drive with 35 seconds to go after Western Michigan kicked a field goal to go up five points. The Broncos' fourth field goal of the game came after Underwood fumbled while trying to scramble for a first down with 1:40 to go.

That turnover was Michigan's third of the game and Underwood's second. He had a rough game and had just 95 passing yards before the final drive.

Western Michigan's offensive stats weren't pretty either, but they controlled the clock. The Broncos had just 221 total yards on 67 plays but held onto the ball for just over 40 minutes. WMU was 8-of-18 on third downs and had 16 first downs to Michigan's 12.

The Wolverines had 276 yards on 48 plays, but committed nine penalties and were just 3-of-10 on third downs.

Had the clock actually expired on the incomplete pass, the first game of coach Kyle Whittingham's tenure would have been an unmitigated disaster. The former Utah coach hired to clean up the mess left behind by the fired Sherrone Moore has a lot to go through when he watches film with his coaching staff.

Instead, Michigan is, somehow, 1-0, and the Big Ten will be doing a lot of explaining in the coming days to show just why the Wolverines deserve to have that win.

articles.title: Michigan's ruling explained: Analyst Terry McAulay presents only theory in which bizarre ending makes sense
articles.summary: Usually, a game is over when the clock hits zero.
articles.body:
The easy word for what happened at the end of No. 16 Michigan's win over Western Michigan is "controversial." That might not work, though, as everyone seems pretty unanimous on what happened.

With only a few seconds on the clock, Michigan attempted a 47-yard Hail Mary that fell incomplete as time seemingly expired. A replay review predictably ensued, with the Big Ten's replay center eventually deciding to put one second back on the clock.

Michigan's second Hail Mary attempt had a better outcome, with the Wolverines pulling off a wild 13-12 win .

However, anyone with the ability to pause and slo-mo the replay shown on television can tell you the clock clearly struck zero while the ball was in the air on the first attempt. The clock should have stopped as soon as Western Michigan safety Micah Davis touched the ball because he had stepped out of bounds. But, again, time expired while the ball was in the air.

There should not have been a final play, as far as any outside observer can tell. It is rare that a blown call feels this obvious, this blatantly irreconcilable with the plain fact of a clock on a screen.

It's not just a bad call, it's a call so bad it leaves us wondering how it's even possible.

There is, however, an explanation of what happened courtesy of NBC officiating analyst Terry McAulay. In the aftermath of the ruling, McAuley went through the replay with the broadcast booth and explained that while the NBC broadcast supposedly had the stadium clock synced up on its replay, the Big Ten's replay center might have had a different sync with its Hawk-Eye camera.

"The ball isn't even close to touching the player when it goes to zero. Now their Hawk-Eye system apparently either was — had a different sync or whatever and they came up with one second when it touched the players. I don't see how that happened, assuming our clock is correct. It is clearly not touching the player. The ball is clearly still in the air when the clock goes to zero on our screen. So the Big Ten's going to have to tell a lot of us how did they get to one second on this play."

That is all speculation, but it at least adds some sort of logic to an irrational sequence of events. It would still make the outcome an outrage, as a clock at the Big Ten replay center in Rosemont, Illinois, would be overruling the clock in Ann Arbor.

We do know one area where McAulay is 100% correct, though: The Big Ten has some explaining to do.

articles.title: Real Madrid suffer Marc Cucurella injury blow ahead of Inter Milan clash
articles.summary: After losing to Real Betis on Friday, Real Madrid are hoping to bounce back when they host Inter Milan in their Champions League opener on Tuesday. Jose Mour...
articles.body:
After losing to Real Betis on Friday , Real Madrid are hoping to bounce back when they host Inter Milan in their Champions League opener on Tuesday. Jose Mourinho failed to win European football's premier competition during his first spell in charge, and that failure will drive him to ensure that he achieves this goal second time around.

If they are to claim La Decimosexta come next June, Real Madrid must ensure they finish inside the top eight in the league phase, as this will see them avoid the jeopardy of the play-off round, which they have featured in on the two occasions since the new format premiered. Getting off to a good start against Inter will be crucial, although Mourinho looks set to be without one of his key players for the match.

In the closing stages of the Betis defeat, Marc Cucurella had to be replaced by Alvaro Carreras. Mourinho revealed in his post-match press conference that the full-back suffered with cramps, but it has since been reported that the 2026 World Cup winner is a major doubt to face the Nerazzurri because of this issue, as per MD .

Carreras poised for return to starting line-up

Cucurella will not be out for long, but the idea is that he does not recover in time to face Inter. Mourinho will know that taking any unnecessary risks with one of his key players would be unwise, which is why Carreras is likely to make his return to the starting line-up, having been left out for the matches against Malaga and Betis.

All being well, Real Madrid will be able to manage without Cucurella for the match against Inter. He should be fine to return for the encounter with Rayo Vallecano next weekend, at which point Los Blancos will try to return to winning ways on the domestic scene.

articles.title: 5 takeaways from Texas A&M’s season-opening shutout win
articles.summary: Going into the season, Texas A&M was viewed by some as a sleeper candidate to win the Southeastern Conference.  Likewise, returning quarterback Marcel Reed i...
articles.body:
Going into the season, Texas A&M was viewed by some as a sleeper candidate to win the Southeastern Conference.

Likewise, returning quarterback Marcel Reed is considered as a darkhorse Heisman Trophy contender.

If Saturday is any indication, Reed and the Aggies may very well cause some commotion in the SEC and national landscape. Reed completed 70% of his passes while throwing for 233 yards and two touchdowns as Texas A&M started its 2026 season with a 50-0 shutout win against Missouri State Saturday night at Kyle Field.

Here are some takeaways from the Aggies performance:

Reed ended his night completing 21-of-30 passes. His second completion resulted in the Aggies' opening TD, a 15-yard strike to Isaiah Horton that finished off A&M's first drive, which went 58 yards in eight plays.

Then late in the first half, Reed threw a strike over the middle to Mario Craver for a 12-yard score, giving A&M a 19-0 advantage.

"I think for the first game, I played well," Reed said postgame. "The team did pretty well. It was a slow start after the first touchdown. … (In the) second half, we bounced back and did what we were supposed to do.

"When you play in the first game of the season, you don't want to show all your stuff. We executed the base plays well enough (Saturday)."

One of A&M's - and Reed's concerns - entering the season was finding a comparable receiver to KC Concepcion, now with the Cleveland Browns.

The Aggies may have found a suitable replacement in Horton, like Concepcion a transfer, in this case coming over from Alabama, and Miami (Fla.) before that. In his Aggies' debut, Horton hauled in four passes for 76 yards.

"My first game as an Aggie was amazing," Horton said. "What I was told about the crowd, especially when we came out, I definitely felt it."

Also, in another bit of irony, Horton is wearing number 7 - which was Concepcion's jersey number last season.

"I thought it was cool that both of our #7 transfers scored the first touchdown of 2025 and 2026," Reed said. "Happy for Zay. I think he's going to be a great guy for us. You saw the vertical threat he can be. … Excited for what's in store for him and us."

While Horton is a newcomer to watch, along with Reed, there are other returning skill standouts at the Aggies' disposal. And they helped contribute to their opening-game showing.

Craver, another one of Reed's key targets, had the most receptions with five along with 41 yards and a TD. Versatile player Terry Bussey caught three passes and had a 10-yard TD run on the opening drive of the second half. Then, returning senior tailback Reuben Owens was the leading rusher with 77 yards on 17 carries.

The Aggies had more than 10 times the number of total yards than it had points. They finished with 505 yards on the night.

Seven different players had a carry, as the Aggies racked up 236 yards on the ground. And then A&M completed 25 passes, which went to 10 different receivers.

A&M was also 50% on third-down conversions (7-of-14) and a perfect 2-of-2 on fourth-down conversions. The Aggies also more than doubled their number of plays compared to the Bears, running 85 total plays to Missouri State's 40.

With Saturday's shutout, it was the first opening-game shutout for A&M since a 24-0 win against LSU in 1993.

A&M held Missouri State to just 67 total yards of offense. The Aggies also forced two turnovers, had one sack and six tackles for loss.

Noah Mikhail, a sophomore linebacker, was the top tackler with seven stops. The sack was recorded by defensive end Ryan Henderson, a San Diego State transfer who also had two TFLs and a forced fumble.

"Happy with how the defense came out and played," A&M coach Mike Elko said. "They played to the level we hoped that they would."

The Aggies also got a safety on special teams, when Missouri State muffed a punt, which squirted into the end zone and out, giving the Aggies a 9-0 lead late in the opening quarter. It was A&M's first safety since 2017.

A&M (1-0) is at home next Saturday to take on Arizona State. Kickoff from Kyle Field is set for 11 a.m.
